notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic drives on the left, a legacy of British rule that also left its mark on signs and road lines.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Both standard white EU plates and UK-style plates with a yellow rear plate; rental cars wear distinctive red plates.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Signs use a unique non-Latin alphabet with softer lowercase shapes than Cyrillic, alongside English.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Bollards have a red reflector at the front and white at the back, triangular with a slanted top, unlike the flat ones in the eastern neighbour.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs look like those of the mainland neighbour, but the local text is written in all capitals.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Town entry signs are a yellow rectangle with a red border or a smaller white one, with the name in two scripts and a speed limit above; unique here.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Tall, dark brown, mostly wooden poles, as in the mainland neighbour.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Pole tops are a crossbar with zero or three insulators, five insulators on the side, or a harp-shaped metal frame; the symmetrical three-insulator top is specific here.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Brightly painted stone buildings with tiled or flat roofs.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mediterranean scenery with bright exposed rock, olive, palm and cypress trees, coastal farmland and pine forest in the mountains.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Houses often have a white horizontal cylindrical water tank with a round lid near one end on top.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Most coverage is smallcam, sometimes with a short antenna visible; the mainland neighbour's smallcam never shows an antenna.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Only the southern half of the island is covered, including two British base areas.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Roads are classed A, B, E and F and grouped by first digit; E and F roads sit near the B road with the same digit.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Four-digit postal codes grouped by region appear on street signs, marked T.K. or T.T.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mostly hilly to mountainous, with the highest ground in the centre.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Bright exposed limestone is mainly along the southern coast.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Reddish soil is found in the interior and northwest.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Vineyards lie more toward the southwest.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Wild yellow mustard bushes are most common in the eastern half.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A forest reserve with winding mountain roads, red soil at the sides and almost no bollards.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: In the northeast a mountain ridge to the north overlooks flat farmland.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The far east is flat with dark red fields and nearly all of it is smallcam coverage, which is rare elsewhere.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Wind turbines cluster west of Larnaca on sandy hills and in a shrubby forest southwest of Anogyra.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: A black-topped bollard like those in Slovenia sometimes appears in the northeast.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Snow-covered roads occur on a few routes in the mountains near a monastery.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Dashed blue lines between outer and inner markings appear on a few roads around the highest mountain.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Banana plantations line the west coast near Peyia.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Many shop signs in Limassol have Russian translations.
